title: Alapin (2.c3) & Smith-Morra (2.d4)
intro: Counter the Alapin (2.c3) with 2...Nf6 and ...d6. Accept the Smith-Morra Gambit (2.d4 cxd4 3.c3) with ...dxc3 and build a solid shield.
variation: e2e4 c7c5 c2c3, e2e4 c7c5 d2d4 c5d4 c2c3

lessons.title: Meeting the Alapin (2.c3)
lessons.summary: Attack e4 with 2...Nf6, hop to d5, and strike with ...d6.

steps.text: With 2.c3, White prepares 3.d4 to build a strong two-pawn centre.
Attack the e4 pawn before White can push d4.
steps.hint: Develop your king's knight to f6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 2...Nf6 to force White to declare their central plans.

steps.text: White pushes past with 3.e5, chasing your knight.
Step forward to a strong central square.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...Nd5: the knight sits actively and keeps an eye on c3.

steps.text: Swap off White's c3 support before challenging e5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...cxd4 to break up White's centre.
steps.ifRight: Now Black strikes at the e5 pawn next.

steps.text: White recaptured 5.cxd4. Strike at the advanced e5 pawn immediately.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...d6 to attack e5 and open your c8 bishop.
steps.ifRight: After 5...d6 6.Nf3 Nc6, Black puts heavy pressure on White's centre.

steps.text: Instead of taking back at once with 5.cxd4, White often develops 5.Nf3 first.
Develop your queen's knight and keep pressure on e5 and d4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Nc6: taking on c3 lets White develop the b1 knight for free.
steps.ifRight: If White takes 6.cxd4, Black strikes back with 6...d6.

steps.ifWrong: Play 6...d6 to undermine White's centre and free your c8 bishop.
steps.ifRight: Black develops ...Bg4 or ...e6 next with a great position.

steps.text: What if White recaptures 5.Qxd4, attacking your d5 knight?
steps.hint: Guard the knight with a pawn that also opens your f8 bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...e6 to defend d5 and prepare ...Nc6, hitting the queen.
steps.ifRight: Next ...Nc6 wins a tempo against White's queen.

steps.text: If White avoids 3.e5 and defends calmly with 3.d3, fight for the centre right away.
steps.hint: Strike in the centre with ...d5 or develop ...Nc6.
steps.ifRight: Black gets an easy, active game.

lessons.title: Meeting the Smith-Morra (2.d4)
lessons.summary: Accept the pawn with ...dxc3 and build a solid shield with ...d6 and ...e6.

steps.text: In the Smith-Morra Gambit, White plays 2.d4 and offers a pawn for quick development.

steps.hint: Take on d4 with your c-pawn.
steps.ifRight: Now White offers the c3 pawn.

steps.text: White plays 3.c3, inviting you to take another pawn.
Accept the gambit cleanly. Keeping the extra pawn with a solid set-up is Black's strongest test.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...dxc3: after 4.Nxc3 Nc6 5.Nf3 d6, Black builds a sturdy shield.
steps.ifRight: You are a clear pawn up. Now develop safely.

feedback.g8f6: 3...Nf6 turns it into an Alapin, which is fine too. 3...dxc3 wins the pawn cleanly.

steps.text: After 4.Nxc3 Nc6 5.Nf3, White prepares Bc4 and O-O.
Build the Scheveningen shield with ...d6 and ...e6 so White's pieces bounce off.
steps.hint: Play ...d6 first to guard e5 and open your c8 bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...d6 (followed by ...e6, ...a6 and ...Nf6) to neutralize White's attack.
steps.ifRight: Next ...e6, ...a6 and ...Nf6 give Black a rock-solid extra pawn.
